exemplars.description: Linear's marketing and app surfaces: near-black neutrals, one restrained violet accent.

why.restraint: Colour is rare and therefore meaningful.
why.temperament: A cool, exact neutral ramp that is recognisably Linear.

exemplars.description: Vercel Geist colour scales: ten gray steps plus functional hues with stated roles.

why.accent-economy: Each functional colour has one documented job.
why.mode-balance: Scales are tuned per mode, not inverted.

exemplars.description: Radix Colors: 12-step scales with paired light and dark sets and role guidance per step.

why.mode-balance: Light and dark scales are designed as pairs.
why.accent-economy: Steps map to roles (background, border, text).

exemplars.description: Stripe on building an accessible colour system: perceptual lightness, contrast-first ramps.

why.temperament: Brand hue kept while meeting contrast.
why.restraint: Hues chosen for function before flavour.

exemplars.description: OpenAI's site: monochrome base where imagery supplies the colour.

why.restraint: The interface stays out of the way of content.

exemplars.description: shadcn themes: the reference variable set and base palettes a candidate starts from (the base, not the reason).

why.accent-economy: The variable roles a candidate must fill, one value each.

exemplars.description: Tailwind v4 default palette in OKLCH: the reference values a brand candidate overrides.

why.temperament: Shows what an unbranded default looks like, the floor a candidate rises from.
